712635.t: Of disputed origin: * Maybe from Proto-Hellenic *twṓmə, from Proto-Indo-European *twoH-mn̥ (“compactness, swelling”), derived from *tewh₂- (“to swell”) + *-mn̥ (“nominal suffix”), and compared with σωρός (sōrós, “heap”).

712604.t: From Proto-Hellenic *skʰíd͏̌d͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *skid-yé-ti, from *skeyd- (“to divide, split”).

712616.t: From Proto-Hellenic *skʰolā́ (“holding back”), perhaps from either Proto-Indo-European *sǵʰ-h₃-l-éh₂ or *sǵʰ-ol-eh₂, in any case derived from the root *seǵʰ- (“to hold”).

712601.t: From Proto-Hellenic *skʰḗmə, from Proto-Indo-European *sǵʰ-éh₁-mn̥, formed from the zero grade of Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold”), synchronically corresponding to ἔχω (ékhō, “to have”) + -μα (-ma).

712697.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tálanton, from Proto-Indo-European *tl̥h₂ent-, from *telh₂- (“to bear, endure”), whence also ἔτλην (étlēn, “to carry, endure”).

712690.t: According to Beekes, probably from Proto-Indo-European *ten- (“stretch”), the same root underlying τείνω (teínō, “to stretch”), though the phonological and morphological details are rather unclear.

712609.t: By surface analysis, σχίζω (skhĭ́zō) + -τός (-tós). Probably from Proto-Indo-European *skidtós, whence also Latin scissus and Proto-Slavic *čistъ.

712605.t: According to Beekes, undoubtedly of Pre-Greek origin.
